text:
marco: Heads-up — noticed weird billing/quota interaction on rerank endpoint when we do model fallback. When primary model OOMs and we fall back, the tenant is charged for both attempts? Anyone seen this?

jess: Saw it in console yesterday. Customer reported a spike in token usage after a canary rollout. :grimacing:

ryan: That shouldn't happen. We should only bill for the final successful invocation. Which code path did it hit — fallback vs parallel fanout?

marco: It's fallback path (sequential). Logs show primary returned 413/oom then we call a smaller model.

dana: Quick note: current quota accounting hooks are per-request start/stop. If we start primary then abort and start fallback we end up double-counting unless we subtract.

samira: Is the fallback initiated by router or by model-serving client? That matters for which component emits the billing event.

ben-ml: Router is initiating fallback. We do a guaranteed attempt on the pinned model, then router calls a compatible variant. Billing events come from serving runtime side — it's counting tokens emitted by each call.

marco: Right, so we count tokens from the dead primary plus the successful fallback. Customer sees two token buckets get charged.

jess: UX question — for console and audit logs, do we want to show both attempts or only the final effective model? Ops wants visibility into failures but billing wants fairness.

elaine: For customers, fairness > raw logs. Show both in diagnostics, but charge only for successful final candidate unless the first produced non-trivial tokens.

ryan: Edgecase: primary might generate partial tokens before OOM. If it produced 20 tokens and then OOMed, are we fine charging for those 20? I think yes.

dana: Agreed. Rule proposal: charge for any tokens actually emitted by a model call. If we fully aborted and no tokens returned, don't charge the attempt. But we need router to signal 'no-output' to billing.

samira: Router currently signals status codes but not token counts. We should extend the internal RPC to include emitted_token_count and terminal_reason.

ben-ml: Implementation sketch:

```
response_meta: {
  emitted_tokens: 0,
  terminal_reason: \"OOM\" | \"TIMEOUT\" | \"SUCCESS\"
}
```

Router will read emitted_tokens and forward a single billing delta per tenant: sum of emitted_tokens across attempts. But we then want billing discounts: if primary had emitted_tokens=0 and terminal_reason != SUCCESS, we should not charge.

marco: Also need to consider for quota enforcement: if primary uses up a tenant's instantaneous concurrency slots but emits zero tokens and we drop it, concurrency usage should be released and not count against rate limits longer than necessary.

jess: Console UX: in the request detail view show a compact waterfall: primary -> fallback, with badges for emitted tokens and terminal reason. By default show only final model and aggregated tokens, with an expand for details.

elaine: And an admin toggle to break down attempts for debug or for billing disputes.

ryan: Telemetry: add an event \"rerank.attempt\" with fields: model_variant, emitted_tokens, terminal_reason, latency_ms, host_region. And a top-level \"rerank.final\" that aggregates.

dana: For sampling, we should only forward full attempt-level payloads for, say, 0.1% of requests to avoid cardinality explosion. But emit the summarized numeric metrics for all requests.

samira: Rollout concern: when we move to compacting billing events, we need backward compatibility with existing telemetry consumers — create a migration window and flag in the console that shows legacy vs compacted billing.

ben-ml: API contract change: add optional response envelope field `attempts` that is an array; default omitted to keep payload small. Example:

```
{
  \"model\": \"re-rank-v2\",
  \"score\": 0.87,
  \"attempts\": [
    {\"variant\":\"v2-large\",\"emitted_tokens\":0,\"reason\":\"OOM\"},
    {\"variant\":\"v2-small\",\"emitted_tokens\":12,\"reason\":\"SUCCESS\"}
  ]
}
```

marco: Good. But we need to be careful: some customers inspect score path output size. Adding attempts by default will break naive parsers. So keep attempts behind a `include_attempts=true` header or a console toggle.

jess: Agreed. New header X-Redwood-Include-Attempts

ryan: Also think about quota semantics when multiple candidates are evaluated in parallel (fanout). We should charge per emitted token across all candidates; but maybe we need a cap for speculative fanout so customers aren't surprised.

elaine: Propose a platform default: speculative fanout is disabled for new tenants, opt-in via tenant flag and explicit quota cap of max speculative tokens per request.

dana: Ops piece: we need a graceful changelog and a migration plan. Ben, Samira — can you two sketch the telemetry and API flag PRs this week?

ben-ml: Can do. I'll open the API PR with the optional envelope and the router changes.

samira: I'll update router+runtime RPCs and add emitted_tokens to the telemetry event. Will also add the sampling config for full attempt payloads.

marco: I'll draft a console mock for the compact waterfall and the admin toggle.

jess: Great. Action items: ben PR for API schema, samira PR for RPC+telemetry, marco console mock, dana to write rollout playbook. We'll sync tomorrow 10:30.

ops-bot: Reminder: scheduled canary deploy at 09:00 UTC tomorrow for rerank routing changes.

ryan: One more thought — enforce a server-side limit that if sum(emitted_tokens_so_far) > tenant_speculative_token_cap, we cancel remaining attempts and return a best-effort result. Prevents runaway charges.

elaine: Yes. Add that to playbook and to the tenant config page in console.

jess: Thanks all. This should keep billing clean and surface enough detail for debugging. :thumbsup:
